points.description: States that a header file stores/contains the class interface (the class declaration), as opposed to the implementation (definitions of member functions), which belongs in the .cpp file.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (1) if it says it holds declarations/class definition generally but does not use the term interface or does not contrast it with the implementation file.

points.description: States that the class interface in the header includes the data members (member variable declarations).
States that the class interface in the header includes member function prototypes (declarations only, not function bodies).

rubric.notes: Full marks need the class interface stated precisely, plus both data members and member function prototypes named. Vague answers (e.g. 'stores code', 'for including libraries', 'organizes the program') earn nothing. Saying the header holds function implementations or definitions is a wrong statement, so the points it affects earn nothing.
